source.title: Some open problems about the solutions of the delay difference equation x_{n+1}=A/x_n^2+1/x_{n-k}^p

accepted.question_text: Let A>0 and consider the positive solutions of the second-order delay difference equation x_{n+1}=A/x_n^2+1/sqrt(x_{n-1}) for n=0,1,..., with arbitrary positive initial values x_{-1} and x_0. Let x_bar be the unique positive equilibrium, i.e. the positive constant solution of the recurrence. For every 0<A<15/4, is x_bar globally asymptotically stable, so that every positive solution converges to this equilibrium?

evidence.quote: Consider the difference equation x n+1 = A/x 2 n + 1/√x n−1, n = 0,1, . . . , (1) where A∈(0,∞) and the initial conditions x−1 and x 0 are arbitrary positive numbers.
Show that when 0< A < 15/4 the positive equilibrium of Eq. (1) is globally asymptotically stable.

accepted.question_text: Let A>0 and consider the positive solutions of x_{n+1}=A/x_n^2+1/sqrt(x_{n-1}) for n=0,1,..., with arbitrary positive initial values x_{-1} and x_0. For every A>15/4, does this recurrence have an asymptotically stable periodic cycle of period two, meaning a nonconstant positive solution alternating between two values?
accepted.context_brief: Stable period-two cycle above the 15/4 threshold

evidence.quote: Consider the difference equation x n+1 = A/x 2 n + 1/√x n−1, n = 0,1, . . . , (1) where A∈(0,∞) and the initial conditions x−1 and x 0 are arbitrary positive numbers.
Show that when A > 15/4 there exists a periodic cycle with period two which is asymptotically stable.

accepted.question_text: Let a>0 and consider the positive solutions of the delay difference equation x_{n+1}=a/x_n^2+1/x_{n-1} for n=0,1,..., with arbitrary positive initial values x_{-1} and x_0. Let x_bar be the unique positive equilibrium of this recurrence. For exactly which values of a is x_bar globally asymptotically stable for all positive initial data?
accepted.context_brief: Global stability for the a/x_n^2+1/x_{n-1} recurrence

evidence.quote: A related difference equation is x n+1 = a/x 2 n + 1/x n−1, n = 0,1, . . . , (16) where a∈(0,∞) and x−1, x 0∈(0,∞).
Open problem 1. (a) For what values of a is the positive equilibrium x̄ of Eq. (16) globally asymptotically stable?

accepted.question_text: Let a>0 and consider x_{n+1}=a/x_n^2+1/x_{n-1} for n=0,1,..., with positive initial values. A period-two cycle for this recurrence is a nonconstant positive sequence r,s,r,s,... satisfying the recurrence. For exactly which values of a is the period-two cycle asymptotically stable, and what is its basin of attraction among positive initial conditions?
accepted.context_brief: Stability and basin of the period-two cycle

evidence.quote: When (18) holds, Eq. (16) has a periodic cycle with period two, {p, q, p, q, . . . }.
Open problem 1. ... (b) For what values of a is the periodic cycle {p, q, p, q , . . . } of Eq. (16) asymptotically stable? What is its basin of attraction?

accepted.question_text: Let A>0, p>0, and k be a nonnegative integer, and consider the delay difference equation x_{n+1}=A/x_n^2+1/x_{n-k}^p for n=0,1,..., with arbitrary positive initial values x_{-k},...,x_0. For which conditions on A, p, and k is the positive equilibrium of this recurrence globally asymptotically stable?
accepted.context_brief: Global stability for the general delay equation

evidence.quote: Eqs. (1) and (16) are special cases of the delay difference equation x n+1 = A/x 2 n + 1/x p n−k n= 0,1, . . . (19) where A, p ∈(0,∞) and k∈ {0,1, . . . }and the initial conditions x−k, . . . , x 0 are arbitrary positive numbers.
Open problem 2. (a) Obtain conditions on A,p and k under which the positive equilibrium of Eq. (19) is globally asymptotically stable.

accepted.question_text: Let A>0, p>0, and k be a nonnegative integer, and consider x_{n+1}=A/x_n^2+1/x_{n-k}^p for n=0,1,..., with arbitrary positive initial values x_{-k},...,x_0. For which conditions on A, p, and k does this recurrence have nonconstant positive periodic cycles of period two; under which of those conditions are the period-two cycles stable; and what are their basins of attraction?
accepted.context_brief: Existence, stability, and basins for period-two cycles

evidence.quote: Eqs. (1) and (16) are special cases of the delay difference equation x n+1 = A/x 2 n + 1/x p n−k n= 0,1, . . . (19) where A, p ∈(0,∞) and k∈ {0,1, . . . }and the initial conditions x−k, . . . , x 0 are arbitrary positive numbers.

Open problem 2. ... (b) Obtain conditions on A,p and k under which Eq. (19) has periodic cycles of period two. Under what conditions on A,p and k are these periodic cycles stable? What is the basin of attraction?

accepted.question_text: Let A>0, p>0, and k be a nonnegative integer, and consider the positive solutions of x_{n+1}=A/x_n^2+1/x_{n-k}^p for n=0,1,..., with arbitrary positive initial values x_{-k},...,x_0. Do there exist nonconstant positive periodic cycles whose minimal period is greater than two?
accepted.context_brief: Higher-period cycles in the general delay equation

evidence.quote: Eqs. (1) and (16) are special cases of the delay difference equation x n+1 = A/x 2 n + 1/x p n−k n= 0,1, . . . (19) where A, p ∈(0,∞) and k∈ {0,1, . . . }and the initial conditions x−k, . . . , x 0 are arbitrary positive numbers.
Open problem 2. ... (c) Do there exist periodic cycles of period greater than two?
